summary: Luise Hercus (1926–2018) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at St Anne's College and the Australian National University. She held positions at St Anne's College, the University of Adelaide, and the Australian National University.
Lungten Dubgyur is a scholar in Tibetology. He completed a graduate degree at Sherubtse College, an LL.B at Government Law College, Mumbai, and an LL.M at the University of Edinburgh.

Lungtok Tenpai Nyima (1927–2017) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Tendzin Lodro Gyatso and at Kyangtsang Monastery. He lectured at the University of Oslo in 1967 and became abbot of Menri Monastery in 1969.
Lungtok Tenpé Nyima studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Lutz Bieg (born 1943) is a Sinologist who earned his doctorate at Heidelberg University and completed his habilitation at the Free University of Berlin. From 1989 to 2008, he served as a professor at the University of Cologne.

Lynn Struve (born 1944) is a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Washington and the University of Michigan before serving on the faculty at Indiana University from around 1977 to 2012.

Lynn Thomas is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees at Lancaster University and a D.Phil from the University of Oxford in 1987. She served as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton, attested in 1997.

Léon Feer (1830–1902) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Etienne Marc Quatremère and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux. He held posts at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, Collège de France, and Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Léon Vandermeersch (1928–2021) was a Sinology and philosophy scholar. Educated at INALCO, the University of Paris, EPHE, and Paris Diderot, he held posts at Aix-Marseille, Paris Diderot, EPHE, the Maison Franco-Japonaise, and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient.

Lê Mạnh Thát (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history. He studied at Saigon University and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later holding a post at Vạn Hạnh University from circa 1974 to 1975.

M. A. Mehendale (1918–2020) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1970, 1983).
M. Athar Ali (1925–1998) was a historian who studied at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1947 to 1961 and subsequently served as a historian there from circa 1953 to 1995.
M. D. Balasubrahmanyam is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested in 1967), where he also completed his dissertation in 1969.

M. H. Krishna (1892–1947) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at Maharaja's College, University of Madras, and University College London under Ernest Arthur Gardner. He held posts at Maharaja's College and the University of Mysore.

M. M. McCabe (born 1948) is a philosopher who studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She held positions at Murray Edwards College, King's College London, University College London, and Newnham College.

M. N. Srinivas (1916–1999) was an Indologist. He studied under M. H. Krishna, G. S. Ghurye, Radcliffe-Brown, and Evans-Pritchard, and held posts at Oxford, Baroda, Delhi, the Institute for Social and Economic Change, and NIAS.

M. R. Raghava Varier (born 1936) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Calicut, Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, and was a professor at the University of Calicut (~1976–1996).

M. S. A. Rao (1926–1985) studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. He held posts at the University of Delhi (~1955–1985), Syracuse University, and the University of Pennsylvania.

M. Seshagiri Sastri was an Indology and linguistics scholar. In 1899, he is attested as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency College, Chennai.
M. Shinoda (born 1977) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Shinoda studied under Seiren Matsunami and attended Agoura High School and the Art Center College of Design.
